This is goal g-33a7a4ae, round 2 (fix round; round 1 was audit-only and already merged as docs/state/silent-failures.md; several fix batches already merged for other files). Read that doc's methodology section first (top of file) and the per-file section for tools/brain-commands.mjs (search for '### tools/brain-commands.mjs' - it lists exact line numbers and the catch form found there: dot-catch-noop-expr, dot-catch-arrow, or try-catch-no-binding).

IMPORTANT - this file is sensitive (MONEY): `haikuFallback` makes a real paid Anthropic API call and records cost to a ledger (`appendLedger`). One flagged catch (`response.json().catch(() => null)`) sits right before the cost-recording logic - read the comment just below it carefully: 'A reply without usage is recorded at the worst case, never at zero.' This means a failed JSON parse is ALREADY designed to fall through to a worst-case cost estimate rather than silently recording zero cost - your fix must preserve this exact fail-safe-toward-overestimate behavior. Add visibility only (log the parse failure), do not touch the worst-case fallback logic, the `known`/`paidUsd` computation, or the `appendLedger` call itself.

The other flagged catches are: an SSH link-open fallback (falls back to null, meaning the Haiku HTTP fallback path is used directly - benign/expected), a best-effort `saved` event-write callback, a best-effort link-close during cleanup, a best-effort response-tail read for diagnostics, and a best-effort triage-result file write. None of these are money-critical themselves - treat them per the normal rules below.

For EACH flagged line in tools/brain-commands.mjs only (do not touch any other file, do not touch the worst-case cost fallback logic described above, do not fix findings in other files even if you notice them while reading):

1. Read the surrounding function to understand what the catch is actually guarding against and what happens today when it swallows silently (what does the function return/do next).
2. Decide, from the real code, whether this catch is:
   (a) An EXPECTED/benign condition - e.g. an SSH link that may legitimately be unavailable, a response body that failed to parse (handled by the worst-case fallback described above), a job response/triage file that may not exist (ENOENT). For these, keep the swallow (do not change control flow or add noisy logging for the expected path), narrow to a specific error code only where one clearly applies, and add minimal visibility (see point 3) for anything else unexpected - same return value, same behavior, just visible.
   (b) A genuinely UNEXPECTED-error catch with no narrower expected case. Add minimal visibility only: a one-line log. This file has no existing logger/journal convention of its own for these catches - use `console.error('[tools/brain-commands.mjs] <short context naming the function/operation>:', error?.message ?? error)`. Do NOT add a throw, do NOT change the function's return value or control flow, do NOT change what happens next.
3. If a catch binds no error variable, add a REAL binding and actually reference it in a console.error call - do not just rename-and-ignore a binding.

Do not refactor anything beyond the flagged catch blocks. Do not reformat unrelated code. Do not rename functions or change exports. Preserve every existing behavior path exactly except for the narrowing/visibility described above - especially the cost-recording path, which must still record the same worst-case cost on a parse failure as before.

Your workspace does not include the test suite, so you cannot run it yourself - the orchestrator runs the real full suite against your output after integration, and will also get this reviewed via the claude CLI before merge given the sensitivity (money/paid-API), and will send back any issue as a follow-up. List, in your final summary, which of the 6 flagged lines you touched, case (a) vs (b), with one line each, and confirm the worst-case cost-recording behavior is unchanged.
